sources.citation: Naitoro, Katerina. 2019. Morphs in search of meaning: Southeast Solomonic transitive morphology in diachronic perspective. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl 1885/163714
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Malango data come solely from her own fieldnotes (Appendix A, p. 355: 'Malango my fieldnotes'); p. 219: 'The descriptions available for SES languages rarely discuss specifics of stress assignment in verbs with longer suffixes'; p. 350 quotes Ross (p.c.) that SES languages have CV syllables and 'unstressed vowels lose little or no quality'. Malango appears only as a 324-item wordlist (no. 57, pp. 128-444, no stress marks) and in the phoneme/sound-correspondence tables (sec. 6.1, pp. 82, 90); a full-text search for stress/accent/penult finds only sound-change footnotes ('in unstressed syllables'), no prosodic statement for any Guadalcanal language.
